channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] Tinned food and three days of bottled water? Fine. But European citizens stockpiling ignores a grim factor: your neighbours will become your enemies
item.description: A friend of mine recently proudly showed me her cellar, stocked with three to four weeks of water and food. “Of course, we’ll be sharing it with the neighbours” she said.But the only thought in my head was “After three to four weeks of no food, no electricity, no internet and no water, you’ll be fighting your neighbours off, no inviting them in.”

item.title: [EU Observer] Caretaker PM Netanyahu expected to escalate violence, as EU sanctions talk on hold until new Israeli government formed
item.description: Israel's "vibrant democracy" gave the most votes to a man wanted for war crimes by the International Criminal Court in The Hague and accused of perpetrating genocide by UN experts, posing questions on whether Israeli society was aligned with EU values.

item.title: [DW] Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
item.description: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

item.title: [EU Observer] Digital panopticon: ‘When you work faster, you have to work even faster’ Amazon workers tell MEPs on AI work surveillance
item.description: Seven MEPs from the employment committee visited Amazon warehouses in Germany and Poland this week - ahead of the EU Commission’s Quality Jobs Act proposal expected in December.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘I don’t care’ about the associate membership label row: Lead MEP Javier Moreno Sánchez on upcoming EU-Canada summit
item.description: “Everybody's focusing on the legal basis of Ursula von der Leyen’s associate membership announcement, but frankly I don't care,” says the European Parliament lead on Canada. He hopes digital trade, critical raw materials and Erasmus+ will be prioritised in talks this week in Montreal.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin faces African anger in Moscow on ‘coercive’ recruits to Russian army in Ukraine
item.description: Russia's hopes of using a summit with African leaders to increase its influence on the continent have been hit by African anger about the fate of their men recruited by the Russian army.

item.title: [DW] EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

item.title: [DW] Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
item.description: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

item.title: [DW] Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
item.description: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

item.description: A new coalition is preparing an anti-dumping complaint, arguing that cheap imports and alleged customs loopholes are putting European producers at risk.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Everything that went wrong with Spain’s high-speed railways
item.description: Spain’s high-speed rail network once embodied the country’s rise as a modern European power. Deadly crashes are raising fresh questions over safety, maintenance and years of investment choices.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Associate’ or ‘ever-closer association’? Semantics aside, what does that leave the EU-Canada love-in?
item.description: German legal precision appears to have prompted the EU to drop its 'associate member' offer to Canada. But on critical minerals, defence and elsewhere, Ottawa and Brussels can still show they are best friends.

item.title: [EU Observer] Corrupt foreign officials should face EU visa-bans and asset-freezes, MEPs and Estonia say
item.description: The anti-corruption bolt-on would have a moral and a strategic value, said Polish rightwing MEP and former interior minister Michał Kamiński, who co-signed the text. "The EU must not become a safe haven for kleptocrats ... that buy loyalty and political influence".

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia unleashes killing spree against Ukrainian civilians on Thursday, targeting children, trains, and buses (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,708)
item.description: Oleshky’s rare ceasefire has let some trapped civilians flee and aid convoys edge in. But now, both armies are racing to fortify positions for the next round of fighting across the Dnipro river.

item.title: [EU Observer] Egypt media crackdown draws ‘lame’ response from EU Commission
item.description: Journalists in Egypt are being jailed and fined in a crackdown that poses questions on the EU's multi-billion deal with Cairo -where human rights are a pre-condition.

item.title: [EU Observer] Bulgaria’s next president must be able to say no to prime minister Rumen Radev
item.description: Rumen Radev’s coalition holds 131 of 240 parliamentary seats in Sofia and backs Iliana Yotova. The next president’s test is not what powers the office holds, but whether it will use them to challenge the government - including over its Black Sea response.

item.title: [DW] European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

item.title: [EU Observer] Campaigners take EU Commission to ombudsman over methane delay, saying it ‘undermines the rule of law’
item.description: The Environmental Investigation Agency accuses the European Commission of maladministration for suspending fines and proposing to delay methane rules for oil and gas importers without evidence they threaten supply.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen : Will Canada ever become an associate member of the EU?
item.description: The EU-Canada summit opens today in Montreal and runs until tomorrow (30 October). One idea is overshadowing the meeting: making Canada an “associate member” of the EU. However, the 27 member states are far from agreed on it.

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

item.title: [DW] In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
item.description: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.
